html:
Gabriel García Moreno was the conservative ruler of Ecuador from 1860 to 1875, president twice and the power behind the presidency between. He tried to build a strictly Catholic nation.

A scientist and lawyer from Guayaquil, he came to power during a civil war and held the country together when its neighbours threatened to divide it. His constitution of 1869 made being Catholic a requirement for citizenship, and in 1873 he dedicated Ecuador to the Sacred Heart of Jesus. He invited religious orders to run schools.

He also built roads, founded a polytechnic school and an observatory, and ruled harshly, exiling opponents. He was hacked to death on the steps of the government palace in Quito in 1875. He and Eloy Alfaro mark the two poles of Ecuador's politics, in the struggle between the Church and the liberals.
sum: Gabriel García Moreno was the conservative ruler of Ecuador from 1860 to 1875, president twice and the power behind the presidency between. He tried to build a strictly Catholic nation.
